newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU says too early to send envoys back to Iran.
newsitem.headline: EU says too early to send envoys back to Iran.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers decided on Monday that the time was not yet right for members of the 15-nation bloc to send their ambassadors back to Iran.
"We noted that the conditions for the return of our ambassadors...have not yet been met," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo told a news conference.

The EU withdrew its ambassadors from Tehran in April following the finding of a German court that senior figures in the Islamic republic's government ordered the assassination of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant in 1992.
Amid the ensuing row, the EU also suspended its so-called critical dialogue with Iran under which it was attempting to bring Iran closer to the West through talks.
Subsequent EU efforts to return ambassadors to Tehran were suspended when Tehran refused to accept the German envoy.

The Islamic republic's President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani said last week Germany would have to wait a while longer before its ambassador could return to Tehran. He indicated the ban would be annulled in time but did not say when.
EU caution over the return of ambassadors to Tehran comes despite softly-softly efforts by Dutch envoys over the weekend to smooth diplomatic feathers.

A senior Dutch foreign ministry official met a series of Iranian officials on Saturday, which Iran's official news agency IRNA said included the Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati and Ali Ahani, director-general for Western Europe at the Iranian Foreign Ministry.
